name: JetBrains Junie

surfaces.label: Junie gateway daemon (Nightly builds only, undocumented): `junie --gateway` starts a detached copy of the same binary with the internal flag `--__run-gateway`, an HTTP server with Slack/voice/loop channels, state under ~/.junie/gateway/ (gateway.lock, config.json holding pid, port, host, version, startedAt). Release builds answer 'The --gateway option is not available in this version. Please use the Nightly build.' Listed first so it is claimed before the tui surface. Note the probe keeps only the outermost matching process, so a gateway spawned by a live TUI can be hidden behind it. Verification 2026-09-29: the --gateway gate message and the launcher constants are present in the STABLE 3419.7 jar too; only the gate is Nightly-specific.

Junie as an ACP agent: the same binary run as `.../Applications/junie.app/Contents/MacOS/junie --acp=true` by an ACP client. Clients: JetBrains IDE AI Chat (Junie by JetBrains from the agent list, downloaded automatically), JetBrains Air (Junie is one of its supported agents), Zed and any editor that reads the ACP registry (cmd ./Applications/junie.app/Contents/MacOS/junie, args --acp=true). The child, not the host app, is the process to watch. The client that spawned it cannot be told from the command line alone; look at the parent pid. Hooks are NOT run in this mode. Where the IDE or Air unpack the download is not documented (an IDE support thread says an `acp-agents` folder in the IDE caches directory).

Junie CLI in a terminal (interactive TUI), and the headless form `junie "task"` / `--task` / `--auth=... "task"` (a headless run is working for as long as it lives). Install shapes all end in the same process: curl installer or Homebrew put a bash shim at ~/.local/bin/junie that `exec`s ~/.local/share/junie/versions/<build>/Applications/junie.app/Contents/MacOS/junie; npm `@jetbrains/junie` is a node wrapper (bin/index.js, spawnSync) around that same shim, so node is the parent and the junie binary is its direct child. During first run or a self-update the shim is a `/bin/bash ~/.local/bin/junie` process, which does not match. The native launcher loads the bundled JVM in-process, so one process, no java child. Matching note (verification): the process specs use path_contains only, no bare `names`: a base name of `junie` alone would also claim any unrelated executable called junie (for example /usr/local/bin/junie of another product), and every documented launch form carries the /junie.app/Contents/MacOS/junie path (shim exec of an absolute path; ACP registry cmd ./Applications/junie.app/Contents/MacOS/junie). Short-lived control invocations `--gateway`, `--gateway-status`, `--gateway-stop` (flags in SystemOptionsGroup, --gateway-status also named in the shim) are excluded like --version and update. A session id can also arrive as a positional `junie://sessions/<id>` link (parameters page), which session_id_args cannot read.

JetBrains Air (macOS app, bundle id com.jetbrains.air inferred from the Homebrew cask zap list; Air.app). Air is a host for Codex, Claude Agent, Gemini CLI, Junie and any ACP agent, so the app itself is not Junie. Its Junie work runs in the `--acp=true` child matched by the ide surface. Air's own process names and where it puts the downloaded agent were not determined.

Junie IDE plugin (org.jetbrains.junie, JetBrains Marketplace 26104) with its own Junie tool window, and the plugin half that ACP agents need for IDE integration. Process shape of the legacy tool-window agent (in the IDE JVM or a child) and its session store were not determined, so there is no process rule and this row cannot see it. Marked as being deprecated in favour of the ACP version by community reports only.

Junie GitHub Action (JetBrains/junie-github-action), Junie GitLab CI/CD, Junie code review on pull requests, and Air cloud tasks: nothing runs on this Mac. Junie Remote mode (/remote) is NOT cloud: the process stays on the Mac and a tunnel mirrors it to the web app.

working_signals.name: Junie is working
working_signals.meaning: Read from the shipped binary, not observed live. Junie takes an IOKit assertion of type PreventUserIdleSystemSleep named 'Junie is working' (IOPMAssertionCreateWithName from MacKeepAwakeService, reason string from KeepAwakeController.WAKE_LOCK_REASON) while any task of the process is running, through KeepAwakeController fed by TaskActivityTracker (a counter of active tasks; the lock is held while the counter is above zero, inferred from the class shape: combine + distinctUntilChanged + collectLatest + awaitCancellation). Owned by the junie pid itself, one per process, so it says the process has a running task but not which of several live sessions. Default keepAwakeMode is WhileTaskRunning; the /settings entry 'Keep awake' (text 'Prevent system sleep while Junie is working', values Off / WhileTaskRunning, stored in ~/.junie/settings.json) can switch it off, and then this signal is silent. Confirmed present in stable build 3419.7 (re-read 2026-09-29: MacKeepAwakeService with IOPMAssertionCreateWithName and PreventUserIdleSystemSleep; the string "Junie is working" in KeepAwakeController$holdWakeLock$2; KeepAwakeMode.WhileTaskRunning); EAP 3479.2 not re-checked. The task counter (TaskActivityTracker) is referenced by JunieSession (TUI), JunieHostBatch and JunieProject; ACP settings carry a keepAwakeMode but no ACP class references the tracker directly, so the assertion in --acp=true processes is unproven. Whether it is dropped while a task waits for approval was not determined. `pmset -g assertions` should list it under the junie pid.

Sessions append one JSON event per line to ~/.junie/sessions/<session-id>/events.jsonl. The exact turn state is in the file, not its mtime: TaskStartedEvent opens a task, a top-level TaskState record closes it (written once per task, also after failures and cancels); every SessionA2uxEvent carries event.state in IN_PROGRESS, INPUT_REQUIRED, COMPLETED, FAILED or CANCELED. Working = the last TaskStartedEvent has no later TaskState, and the last event.state is IN_PROGRESS. A write can raise working but a quiet file never proves idle (long model calls write nothing); keep an open task working only while its junie pid is alive. Record kinds and key names taken from a third-party reader's fixtures and source, the schema is unversioned.

Inferred from bytecode, not observed. Each shell tool call is a fresh direct child of the junie process: `bash -lc '<command> ...' </dev/null` (JVMSpawnShellExecutionEnvironment, BashShellType), prefixed on macOS with a perl one-liner (`use POSIX qw(setsid); setsid(); exec @ARGV`) or nohup that exec()s into the shell, so the child shows as a shell. State (cwd, env, jobs) is captured by markers appended to each command, not by a long-lived shell. bash may exec a single simple command directly, in which case the child carries the tool's name and not a shell name. Blind while the model streams. User-configured MCP servers are also direct children and long-lived; only shell names count here.
Unmeasured guess. The process is a JVM running a Compose-based terminal UI, so an idle baseline was not seen; raise the floor after a live run.

waiting_signals.meaning: Junie stamps INPUT_REQUIRED on the session while it is blocked on the human: a command approval (TerminalBlockUpdatedEvent with an approval request), a question (AskAsyncRequestUpdatedEvent), or a choice (ChoiceRequestUpdatedEvent). It clears when the same step leaves INPUT_REQUIRED, or on UserAsyncResponseEvent, UserResponseEvent, CancelAgentEvent or TaskState. This is the only outside-readable wait signal in every surface, including ACP hosts. In the TUI it is shown as 'Awaiting input' in /history (statuses Working…, Awaiting input, Ready).

Fires just before a permission dialog would show (Bash, Edit, Read, MCP tool names), TUI host for certain (the hooks page lists it under the TUI in one paragraph and under TUI and batch in Limitations), Early Access per the docs. Caution: a hook that exits 0 without a blocking decision APPROVES the action and skips the dialog, so a monitor-only hook must not exit 0; exit 2 or decision deny auto-denies; another non-zero exit falls back to the dialog with a warning notification. There is no Notification event and no idle event, so hooks alone give no clean observe-only wait signal.

The TUI writes a terminal notification 'Junie needs your input' (OSC 9, OSC 777 notify or OSC 99, protocol chosen by TerminalNotifier) and 'Junie finished' on task completion, and can set the terminal title with OSC 0. Seen in class constants only: what gates it (the enabled flag, terminal focus) and whether the title carries a status glyph were not determined. Read from the terminal host, not from ps.

hooks.config: hooks object in ~/.junie/config.json (or $JUNIE_HOME/config.json), or in a file passed with --config-location; hooks/hooks.json inside an installed extension. <project>/.junie/config.json hooks are ignored by default. Shell command hooks run via sh -c. Only the interactive TUI and batch hosts run them: ACP hosts (JetBrains IDE AI Chat, Air, Zed) and server hosts do not. Docs tag hooks as Early Access ('To try it, install the Early Access version of Junie CLI'); the stable 3419.7 jar contains HooksConfiguration, but an Env.hooksEnabled flag exists and its value for the Release channel was not determined, so treat hooks as EAP-only until seen on a stable install. UserPromptSubmit fires in the interactive TUI only; the docs list PermissionRequest under the TUI in one paragraph and under TUI and batch in the Limitations section.

telemetry.how: No OpenTelemetry export found: no io.opentelemetry classes, no OTEL_ or OTLP strings in the stable 3419.7 and EAP 3479.2 application jars, nothing in the docs. JetBrains anonymous usage statistics exist (settings.json shareAnonymousStatistics, --share-anonymous-statistics, JUNIE_SHARE_ANONYMOUS_STATISTICS) and /feedback uploads logs; neither is an OTLP stream. Session events in events.jsonl are the only structured local stream.

notes: Nothing here was seen on a live instance: Junie is not installed on this Mac and I did not run any downloaded binary. The strongest facts are structural (paths, bundle id, hook events, sidecars, event schema, state enum). The strongest working signal, the 'Junie is working' sleep assertion, is read from bytecode constants and is the first thing to check on a live run (`pmset -g assertions | grep -i junie` during a turn, then during an approval prompt). One process is not one session: /new and IDE window reuse mean one junie pid can serve several sessions, so map a process to its session with ~/.junie/processes/<pid>-*.json (newest startedAt wins, body authoritative, file usually survives exit per a third-party capture, but the binary has latch cleanup code, so a missing file proves nothing), `--session-id` (or a positional junie://sessions/<id> link, not readable by session_id_args) only appears on resume, and fall back to the process cwd matched against projectDir in ~/.junie/sessions/index.jsonl. events.jsonl can grow large (open YouTrack item JUNIE-5070), so tail it, and never read message text. Matching reads the command line only: the process name is `junie` in every surface, and the ide, tui and daemon surfaces differ only by an argument (--acp, --__run-gateway), so keep the surface order daemon, ide, tui. Paths with a space (an ACP client could unpack under Application Support) are cut at the space by the probe, which would lose both the name and path match. Direct children only: user MCP servers are long-lived direct children, shells are per command. Adversarial verification 2026-09-29: re-read the docs pages, ACP registry entry, install shim, npm wrapper, Homebrew formula and the 3419.7 zip/jar; confidence stays documented (cap for a harness not installed here). Repaired: bare `names` removed (false positive on any executable called junie), `--gateway`, `--gateway-status`, `--gateway-stop` excluded from the tui surface (verified on synthetic ps lines against tools/agents_probe.py), hooks marked Early Access, wrong Reddit URL fixed. Still unproven and treat as guesses: the assertion in ACP processes, the 3% CPU floor on a JVM UI, and whether a single-command bash -lc execs into the tool name.
